question: Should OpenClaw expose channel delivery failures to agents as queued system events, as message-tool result status, or through another typed delivery outcome contract?
rationale: The next step changes shared agent/channel semantics, prompt context, retry behavior, transcript state, error redaction, and plugin SDK expectations, so automation should not choose the product/API shape.

options.title: Define a shared typed contract
options.body: Create a maintainer-approved delivery outcome contract and wire it through agent runtime, message tool, and channel/plugin SDK boundaries before implementing per-channel handling.

options.title: Keep scoped diagnostics only
options.body: Leave current CLI/task/cron/channel diagnostics in place and close or split this broad request into narrower transport bugs.

options.title: Limit to system-event injection
options.body: Implement queued system-event notification for failed delivery only, accepting that retry and tool-result semantics may need later follow-up.

recommendation.title: Define a shared typed contract
recommendation.body: Create a maintainer-approved delivery outcome contract and wire it through agent runtime, message tool, and channel/plugin SDK boundaries before implementing per-channel handling.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest current history on shared outbound delivery and agent deliveryStatus code, making him the best available routing owner for the contract decision.
